Asha (ML Eng): FYI - after onboarding ranker-slim-2b-q4 with async-prefetch enabled, short-query NDCG dropped ~2.6% vs baseline and we see nondeterministic topk permutations across reruns.
Jordan (Eval): Can you share the exact commands and a tiny example where ordering flips?
Asha (ML Eng): Repro (local shadow run):
```
./bin/shadow_run --model ranker-slim-2b-q4 --slice short_queries --batcher async-prefetch --seed 2026 --kvcache=false
# cfg overrides:
# runtime.prefetch_async=true
# runtime.kv_spill=16384
```
Example run outputs:
```
run1.topk: [1012, 34, 7, 89]
run2.topk: [34, 1012, 7, 89]
metrics (short_slice): ndcg@10 0.673 -> 0.655, mrr@10 0.441 -> 0.447
```
Jordan (Eval): So NDCG down, MRR slightly up. That pattern usually means head rank positions swapped but top-1 got better sometimes. Could be tiny float noise in dot prod or a different prune order upstream. Did anything change in candidate pruning or the CPU scorer?
Asha (ML Eng): Two recent diffs: we landed q4 per-channel scales in runtime/quant/scale-updates and Rafael's team toggled prefetch async to reduce cold IO. My hunch: quantized scale/rescale + async reorder of batch execution introduces microsecond scheduling jitter that changes rounding path.
Rafael (Infra): The async-prefetch rollout was yesterday (infra-roll/221). It uses a worker pool to prefetch KV and may reorder fetch completion. We intentionally allowed out-of-order responses to reduce tail latency.
Tess (Prod): Is this manifesting in canary traffic or only offline? If canary, what percentage and do we pause?
Asha (ML Eng): Observed in shadowbench and also small canary at 3% — we've paused auto-roll for that model but traffic already hit.
deploy-bot: Snapshot created -> s3://redwood-shadows/3478901234-ranker-slim-q4-logs.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Jordan (Eval): Quick experiments to isolate: 1) run q4 with prefetch disabled, 2) run q8 with prefetch enabled, 3) run q4 with deterministic tie-breaker in scorer (stable sort by candidate id). If ordering normalizes with deterministic tie-breaker, it's likely FP nondeterminism.
Asha (ML Eng): Plan executed: starting ablation now. Commands:
```
# ablation set A: quantization effect
./bin/shadow_run --model ranker-slim-2b-q8 --batcher async-prefetch --seed 2026 --kvcache=false
# ablation set B: prefetch effect
./bin/shadow_run --model ranker-slim-2b-q4 --batcher serial --seed 2026 --kvcache=false
# ablation set C: deterministic tie-breaker
patch scorer: if abs(score_a-score_b) < 5e-7 then compare candidate_id
```
Rafael (Infra): I can temporarily gate prefetch to be in-order for the canary fleet if you want to test a quick mitigation without full rollback. Low-risk toggle.
Tess (Prod): Yep please do that if ablation indicates prefetch is the issue. Keep prod informed on expected latency impact.
Jordan (Eval): If deterministic tie-breaker brings NDCG back within noise but MRR changes inversely, we should add a short-query safety net in the service layer: if slice == short and ndcg deviation > 1.5% then fallback to stable-sorting scorer.
Asha (ML Eng): Early ablation results (20m):
- q8 + async-prefetch: ndcg@10 0.672 (baseline 0.673) mrr@10 0.442
- q4 + serial-batcher: ndcg@10 0.671 mrr@10 0.441
- q4 + deterministic-tiebreak: ndcg@10 0.672 mrr@10 0.440
Interpretation: q8 seems fine, q4 tends to show slight jitter but serial batching reduces flip frequency; deterministic tie-breaker stabilizes NDCG. Points to quantization amplifying small nondeterminism from prefetch interleaving.
Rafael (Infra): I'll flip prefetch to in-order on the canary nodes for ranker-slim-2b-q4 and monitor. If that stabilizes metrics we'll coordinate a config change across fleets.
Tess (Prod): Good. Also add a short smoke-check in the deploy checklist to assert stable topk ordering for a fixed seed post-deploy.
Asha (ML Eng): Will add that and open an RFC for a conservative fallback path in scorer for short queries. Also will prepare a deterministic embedding dump for a failing seed so we can diff scale factors across runs if needed.
Jordan (Eval): Thanks. If you upload the dumps to the snapshot, I'll run a per-dimension delta and check for scale factor oscillation.
Asha (ML Eng): Uploaded dumps to s3 path above. Will follow up after Rafael confirms the in-order canary run. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
